_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: issue #208 (diagnosis and live-tenant measurements by @geekbrownbear, superseding PR #215), plus an adversarial Codex review of the reprint diff. This ledger was created during the 4.24.0 -> 4.30.2 reprint, and its absence is exactly why that reprint silently dropped the multi-tenant header wiring, the ThreatLocker doctor diagnosis, the novel-command registrations AND six implemented novel commands (replaced by TODO scaffolds that still answered --help). Every entry below was verified to fail check_handfixes.py when reverted. A reprint recipe lives at skills/threatlocker/reprint-patches.py: run it after `printing-press generate --spec <spec> --research-dir <dir>` and the -pp- strip to replay every patch below without rediscovering them by hand.

handfixes.summary: sync's canonical resources map to ThreatLocker's real list endpoints, and resources that cannot enumerate are kept out of the default sync set
handfixes.why: The 4.30.2 engine generates the whole POST sync path correctly from the spec (method, paged body, id_field). Two profiler behaviours still need correcting. FIRST, applySyncCandidates picks which candidate owns the CANONICAL resource name by SHORTEST PATH, so the portal's picker endpoints win: /Computer/ComputerGetForNewComputer is 3 characters shorter than /Computer/ComputerGetByAllParameters, and /Organization/OrganizationGetForMoveComputers is shorter than the child-organizations route. The real list is then parked under a sibling name, so rows land in a sibling table while devices health, search, analytics and every --data-source local read keep reading the empty canonical tables. (computers install-info only becomes a candidate at all because profiler.containsAny does SUBSTRING matching and "inst-ALL-info" contains the list term "all".) SECOND, the generated default set shipped resources that cannot enumerate: the computer-groups dropdown twin duplicated computer-groups into a second table, scheduled-actions always answers HTTP 417, and audit resolved to a by-file-path detail route. Verified against a local fixture: a full default sync stores 225 rows across all eight resources in their canonical TYPED tables (computers 58, organizations 7, applications 23, approvals 11, computer-groups 4, online-devices 9, tags 1, versions 112), and a 250-row fixture walks pages 1-3 without truncation. Before the fix the shipped 0.1.1 stored 0 rows for all 9 resources while exiting 0. Two more resources were recovered the same way in #223. scheduled-actions resolved to GET /ScheduledAgentAction/List, which answers HTTP 417 'Invalid Scheduled Agent Action Type provided' unless a scheduledType flat sync cannot know is supplied; the real collection is the paginated POST /ScheduledAgentAction/GetByParameters, which lost the canonical name on path length. reports returns CATEGORIES ({categoryName, reports}) rather than individual reports, so the row key is the category name; without it every row failed id extraction.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press should not choose the canonical sync resource by shortest path: prefer the endpoint the spec names `list`, or let a spec key nominate the sync source explicitly. profiler.containsAny should match on word/segment boundaries so "install-info" stops being classified as a list endpoint via the substring "all". Filed upstream as part of the #208 retro.

handfixes.summary: one shared helper injects the ManagedOrganizationId / OverrideManagedOrganizationId headers on BOTH the CLI and MCP surfaces, and the response cache is partitioned by tenant
handfixes.why: Most ThreatLocker Portal API data calls are scoped by the ManagedOrganizationId header, which the press does not generate from the spec's auth block. Three defects, all of which an MSP would hit. (1) The 4.30.2 reprint dropped the whole CLI wiring (rootFlags field, persistent flag, header injection) because no ledger asserted it. (2) The injection only ever lived in rootFlags.newClient, so the MCP server -- which builds its client in newMCPClientFromConfig and never touches rootFlags -- issued every live call with NO tenant scoping at all, silently, on a connector whose entire premise is many customer tenants. (3) client.cacheKeyFor hashes the token plus a representation-header whitelist that excludes both tenant headers, so two --org invocations sharing a path, params and token collided on one cache entry and served tenant A's rows to a request targeting tenant B for the life of the cache TTL. tenant_scope.go is now the single source of truth for (1) and (2); tenantScopeCacheHeaders partitions the cache for (3), guarded by TestCacheKeyPartitionsByTenant, which fails with an identical key across tenants when the partitioning is removed.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press should support a spec-declared per-request tenant header (name + env var + flag) so per-tenant scoping is generated for every surface, and should treat any such header as cache-partitioning rather than leaving it to the representation-header whitelist.

handfixes.summary: sync refuses to report success when it stored nothing this run, when the API declared failure, when enumeration ended abnormally, or when rows landed only generic tables
handfixes.why: #208's real damage was not that sync failed, it was that sync failed SILENTLY: it printed sync_complete and exited 0 with an empty store for months. Three paths could still do that after the endpoint fix. (1) UpsertBatch's `stored` counts GENERIC resources rows and downgraded typed-table failures to a stderr line, so every typed row could fail while sync reported a healthy count and the typed tables that power devices health, applications hunt and analytics stayed empty. UpsertBatchDetailed now returns typedFailures and sync surfaces it. (2) A resource that consumed items but stored none only emitted an anomaly event and still aggregated as success. (3) A walk that ended abnormally (non-JSON 200, stuck cursor) also aggregated as success. All three now return a Warn, so the run reports warned instead of success. Verified against a fixture returning rows with no extractable primary key: the run reports success:0 warned:1 where the shipped 0.1.1 reported success:8 warned:0 with an empty store. A second adversarial review found three more paths to the same silent success. (4) The zero-row guard originally tested db.Count(resource), the size of the WHOLE mirror including earlier syncs, so a resource that stored nothing today passed because yesterday's rows were still there; it now tests rows stored by this run, and sync_complete reports `stored` alongside `total`. (5) A 200 body declaring its own failure ({"success":false,"data":null}) was classified by the generated empty-page check as a legitimate empty page, ending the walk "complete", advancing the watermark and reporting a clean sync on an API error; responseReportsFailure now ends the walk abnormally instead. (6) A failed resume checkpoint returned "saving sync progress for ..." while the critical-error classifier only recognised "saving sync state for ", so a broken checkpoint could still exit 0 alongside another successful resource. (7) `workflow archive` logged each per-resource error and warning and then reported resources_synced equal to the FULL resource list and returned nil, so the same false success survived one command over; archiveOutcomeError now gates its exit status and the JSON payload reports archived/warned/errored separately.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press should treat 'consumed rows but stored none', 'typed-table projection failed' and 'enumeration ended abnormally' as first-class non-success outcomes in the generated sync aggregation, rather than anomaly events layered on a success return.

handfixes.summary: the seven hand-authored novel commands keep their real implementations and their wiring into the command tree
handfixes.why: Two distinct ways a reprint silently guts these. FIRST, wiring: before 4.30.2 the registrations were hand-edits inside generated parents (applications.go, approvals.go, audit.go, root.go), so every regeneration unregistered the commands while leaving their source on disk. novel_commands_register.go now registers `applications hunt` through the generator's own novelCommandHooks mechanism, which runs after the generated tree is built and therefore survives regeneration. SECOND, and worse: generating WITH --research-dir makes the press emit the other six novel commands as TODO SCAFFOLDS whose RunE returns `TODO: implement novel feature`. Those scaffolds still register and still answer --help, so a smoke test that only walks --help passes while devices health, approvals triage, approvals approve-batch, audit drift, audit export and audit retention-check all error at runtime. That is the connector's entire headline surface, including the devices health rollup that #208 is about. The implementations are grafted from the prior print; these markers assert real bodies rather than scaffolds. huntWhereClause is kept private to applications_hunt.go because the shared whereClause it used to call lived in the pre-4.30.2 hand-authored audit_export.go.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press should not regress an implemented novel command to a TODO scaffold on regeneration when the prior print carries a real body; and `verify` should execute a novel command's RunE rather than accepting a --help response as proof it works.

handfixes.summary: doctor validates the raw 64-hex token format, reports the ManagedOrganizationId state, and maps a 401/403 to its likely ThreatLocker cause
handfixes.why: This is the connector's headline diagnostic and the answer to the #1 ThreatLocker integration complaint (cryptic 401s from a Bearer-prefixed or idle-expired token, or a missing org header). Both cli/internal/cli/which.go and cli/internal/mcp/tools.go advertise doctor as doing exactly this, so when the reprint dropped the block (as 4.30.2 did) the CLI advertised a capability it no longer had. isTLTokenWellFormed and tlAuthDiagnosis live in the novel file threatlocker_novel.go; these markers assert the generated doctor.go still calls them.

handfixes.summary: doctor verifies the credential against a command that actually reaches the API - now by RUNNING an argument-free GET probe rather than suggesting a command and hoping
handfixes.why: The generated suggestReadCommand returns the FIRST leaf that looks like a read, which for ThreatLocker is `applications get`. That command requires --application-id, and the generator deliberately prints help rather than pflag's terse error on a bare invocation, so it exits 0 without ever touching the API. An operator follows doctor's own instruction, sees a clean exit, and concludes their credentials are fine. That is not hypothetical: it cost the reporter of #208 a diagnostic cycle and they filed it as #217. isSuggestableReadLeaf cannot tell the difference because the requirement is enforced inside RunE - no annotation, no MarkFlagRequired, no positional in Use. threatlockerVerifyCommand names a command that runs, falling back to the generic 'run any read command' message rather than naming a broken one. TestDoctorVerifyCandidatesAreRunnable drives each candidate against a fixture and fails if it makes no HTTP request, so asserting mere existence (which the broken suggestion also satisfied) cannot pass. SUPERSEDED-IN-PLACE 2026-08-25 (issue #282): the intent is unchanged and now enforced more strongly. doctorProbeCredentials (cli/internal/cli/doctor_verdict.go) replaces both suggestReadCommand and threatlockerVerifyCommand at the doctor call site. It requires pp:method GET and a concrete argument-free pp:path, so it structurally cannot pick `applications get` (positional/required-flag shapes are rejected) - and it cannot pick any of the three doctorVerifyCandidates either, because all three are POST, which this ledger entry did not previously catch. Most importantly it no longer SUGGESTS a command for the operator to run: it issues the authenticated GET itself and reports what came back, so an operator can no longer mistake a clean exit for a working credential. tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py drives the real binary against a stub in four states and fails if doctor claims health while the credential is rejected or the base_url is wrong.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press should annotate required-flag commands so isSuggestableReadLeaf can see them, and rank candidates instead of taking the first alphabetically. Affects 38 connectors' generated doctor.go. DONE UPSTREAM: mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4489 merged 2026-09-01 and first shipped in press v4.31.5 - endpoint and promoted commands now emit pp:requires-input and doctor skips those leaves. Tracker provenance: finding 3 of #4482 (now closed by that PR), originally item 7 of #4165, which was closed as completed with this finding explicitly out of scope - do NOT cite #4165 as open. This connector was generated on 4.30.2, so the hand-fix is still load-bearing today. Retiring it at the next reprint is a deliberate decision, not automatic: the upstream fix makes the SUGGESTED command runnable, which is weaker than doctorProbeCredentials issuing the authenticated GET itself.

handfixes.summary: the MCP tenant gate falls through to the tool handler when no platform source is registered, instead of default-denying every non-mirror tool
handfixes.why: cli.VerifyMCPInvocation returns (nil, nil) when registeredPlatformSource is nil, which means 'there is nothing to gate' - and no connector in this repo registers a platform source (registerPlatformSource has zero callers outside internal/cli/platform_client.go). The 4.30.1/4.30.2 gate read that nil session as a failure and answered 'MCP tenant gate is not configured' for every tool that is not a Cobra mirror. Cobra mirrors carry pp:tenant-gate = "child-cli" and pass through, so the damage was invisible in a tool count: 6 tools per connector were dead while the server still listed them. Those 6 are the entire offline-mirror surface (context, search, sql) plus the entire code-orchestration surface (<prefix>_search / _get / _execute) - exactly the capabilities this connector's own description says a plain read-only MCP does not ship. Measured over stdio before the fix: 6/6 returned isError with the gate message; after, all 6 reach their handler. Fixed upstream in cli-printing-press 4.30.3 (issue #4157, PR #4171); this is the surgical back-port, byte-identical to what 4.30.3 emits. TestMCPUngatedInvocationUsesRealVerifier is the regression test that ships with the 4.30.3 template: it drives the wrapper with the REAL verifier (not the fake the other two tests install) and fails if the handler is blocked. Reverting either the fall-through or the test fails check_handfixes.py.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Already fixed in the press at 4.30.3 (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4171). A reprint on 4.30.3 or later regenerates both the fall-through and the conformance test, so this entry exists to keep the back-port from being dropped by a reprint on an older engine or by a regen-merge that resurrects the 4.30.2 body.

asserts.not_contains: NewToolResultError("MCP tenant gate is not configured")

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For threatlocker the manifest gained: THREATLOCKER_API_KEY, THREATLOCKER_BASE_URL, THREATLOCKER_ORG_ID, THREATLOCKER_USER_AGENT. server.json gained: THREATLOCKER_API_KEY, THREATLOCKER_BASE_URL, THREATLOCKER_ORG_ID, THREATLOCKER_USER_AGENT. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: THREATLOCKER_API_KEY, THREATLOCKER_BASE_URL, THREATLOCKER_ORG_ID, THREATLOCKER_USER_AGENT. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: `recall` and `playbook list` are annotated mcp:local-write, not mcp:read-only, because both open the writable learn store and record a row (issue #275 finding 4)
handfixes.why: issue #275 finding 4. `recall` (teach.go) declared mcp:read-only=true, opened the WRITABLE store via store.OpenWithContext and inserted a learn event on every call; `playbook list` (teach_playbook.go) was marked read-only and appended an audit record. The annotation is what an MCP host reads to decide what to auto-approve, so a false one is the same defect class as a doctor command that reports credentials fine without ever checking them: the promise, not the write, is the harm. The replacement is mcp:local-write, a tier this same engine already defines and already uses for `teach` and `playbook amend`: writes land only in the CLI's own local store, never in external state and never in a user-visible file, so the walker registers destructiveHint=false and openWorldHint=false while leaving readOnlyHint unset. Measured at the live MCP server before and after: recall and playbook_list went from readOnlyHint=true, openWorldHint=true to readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false, openWorldHint=false. AGENTS.md is press-generated and carried the same claim in prose, so the annotation sentence there was regenerated from the booted server's tools/list and is pinned by the AGENTS.md asserts below. This is a TRUTH fix, not a behaviour fix - the RunE bodies are untouched and both commands still write exactly what they wrote before. Upstream closed this wontfix (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so a reprint reintroduces the false annotation and this ledger is the only thing that catches it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Upstream declined (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so there is nothing to encode in the press today. If that is ever revisited, the rule is mechanical rather than a judgement call: a command whose RunE reaches store.OpenWithContext, appendLearningsAudit or any Insert must not carry mcp:read-only. `learnings list`, `learnings candidates` and `learnings stats` are the remaining teach-loop siblings: each still carries mcp:read-only and each still opens the writable store (creating the database file, running migrations and tightening file modes) though none records a row, and all three were left alone deliberately because the ratified decision named only `recall` and `playbook list`. The same shape is not confined to the teach loop: every command that reads this connector's local mirror opens it through the same read-write call, `analytics` included, so what the press should encode is the mechanical rule above rather than a per-command list.

handfixes.summary: MCP discovery exposes executor-facing request schemas and indexes input names and known enum values
handfixes.why: Issue #351: endpoint summaries omitted required request inputs. Keep canonical JSON body case and nesting, path/header/query routing, and exact short request search terms. Contracts are derived from the shipped CLI source, and the existing CLI commands and auth remain intact. Upstream request metadata fix #4890 was not merged when this surgical repair was made.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Replace this downstream contract extraction only when a released Printing Press generates equally complete executor-facing schemas and preserves every existing hand-fix.

handfixes.summary: One decoded output funnel for every server text the client shows, applied by tools/maintainer/apply_secret_funnel.py: maskCredentialText still masks each held credential as written and URL-escaped, then withholds the WHOLE text if a held value survives in any view of it (control characters, JSON and JavaScript escapes, the identity escape, percent, HTML entities, tags, base64 and hex, searched breadth-first and capped by total work; cliutil.FunnelWithhold, shared byte-identical across the fleet). The API error body is checked whole before the display cut; the 2xx HTML summary and the token mint, refresh and auth login error bodies are funnelled when present; the client holds its credentials when built and its resolved auth header on every request; every command error before Cobra prints it, every JSON/agent error envelope, and every MCP error result pass the same funnel over everything the process holds. Success output is never funnelled.
handfixes.why: class_harness.py secret-echo drives the built CLI and MCP server against a fake server that reflects each configured credential in every encoding; before press 4.34.0 the generated masks cover only the raw, QueryEscape and PathEscape forms (cli-printing-press #5145), so a fresh print fails it. Press 4.34.0 (#5169) masks encoded forms too; the funnel stays for the connector's hand-written code (token endpoints, novel commands), which the generated masks never see. Matching encoded needles one at a time never converged in review, so the fix is a decode-then-check backstop that withholds the whole text and fails closed (text over 1 MiB or work past the cap is withheld). The withheld notice keeps the auth reading of an auth failure, so exit codes still classify. Known limits: values under 8 characters are only masked as written; case-changed, split-and-interleaved, compressed or encrypted echoes are not reconstructed. A reprint that drops these edits fails class_harness.py secret-echo in CI and these asserts; re-run tools/maintainer/apply_secret_funnel.py --slug <slug>.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cli-printing-press issue #5145 (encoded credential echo). The generated maskCredentialText should end in a decode-then-check backstop over every held credential, and the error-body and token-endpoint paths should check the whole body before the display cut.

hand_wired.class-test: Every ThreatLocker list is a POST search, so the harness's argument-free GET sample never reaches the client. Proven instead with class_harness's reflecting HTTP 403 server (every credential in every encoding, body and headers) against the POST reads computers list, organizations list, approvals list and applications search in --json and --agent, and the MCP threatlocker_read tool on computers.list, organizations.list and approvals.list: every request reached the server and no encoding of the credential survived in stdout, stderr or the MCP result.

handfixes.summary: tl_path_helpers.go declares replacePathParam and pathParamSegmentValue, which the generated dependent sync calls but helpers.go only emits when the spec has path params
handfixes.why: helpers.go.tmpl emits the two helpers only under .HasPathParams, while sync.go.tmpl calls them for every dependent resource, so a spec with no path params and a query-keyed dependent does not compile. Delete the file when the press emits them: a duplicate declaration at build time is the signal.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press: emit replacePathParam and pathParamSegmentValue whenever sync.go references them, not only under .HasPathParams.

handfixes.summary: the application-files dependent syncs under the name the store's typed dispatch knows, so its rows reach the typed application_files table that applications hunt reads
handfixes.why: The profiler names the dependent application_files; the store's typed dispatch knows only application-files, so every row reached the generic table, the typed table stayed empty, and no failure counter fired (measured on a local fixture: 46 generic rows, 0 typed). The rename (keys, cases, Name:) matches the shipped sync name. TestEveryDependentLandsInItsTypedTable fails on the raw 4.34.0 render.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press: derive the dependent resource name with the same normalization the store's typed dispatch uses.

handfixes.summary: approvals approve-batch performs live approvals only with --yes; without it the command previews and sends nothing
handfixes.why: The command performs cross-tenant approval writes. It ran them without --yes although every example showed the flag. The MCP mirror blocks --yes, so an MCP caller can only preview. TestApproveBatchRefusesWithoutYes was seen failing before the fix.

handfixes.summary: doctor's credential probe skips commands that need input, so a healthy install is not reported as a wrong base_url
handfixes.why: The probe picked applications get, which needs --application-id, so a healthy install read 'base_url is not this vendor's API root'. The probe now skips leaves annotated pp:requires-input and leaves with a required flag. TestDoctorProbeNeedsNoInput was seen failing before the fix.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Fleet: doctorProbeableLeaf in doctor_verdict.go should skip any leaf with required input on every connector.

handfixes.summary: doctor treats the shipped base URL (instance g's real API root) as a real host, and reserves the whole example TLD rather than one literal host
handfixes.why: portalapi.g.threatlocker.com is a real API root, so treating it as a placeholder told a working operator to set a base URL. RFC 2606 reserves the whole .example TLD; press 4.34.0's novel-host gate cannot resolve the literal localhost.example and failed dogfood.

handfixes.summary: the unused endpointPositionalArgs helper cluster is removed from helpers.go while nothing calls it
handfixes.why: With no positional params in the spec, helpers.go's endpointPositionalArgs cluster (5 functions) is dead and dogfood fails '5 dead helper functions found'. Restore the cluster if a positional param is added.

handfixes.summary: with the local-data opt-out set, the process never claims the default store
handfixes.why: The generated claim check considered only claimSuppressed, so a run with THREATLOCKER_NO_LOCAL_DATA set could still claim and create the default store. TestLocalDataOptOutNeverClaimsTheDefaultStore was seen failing before the fix.

handfixes.summary: local-store novel reads filter on the explicit --org only, and approvals approve-batch writes only to the tenant the operator chose (--org, else THREATLOCKER_ORG_ID) or to every tenant with --all-tenants, refusing a live run with neither
handfixes.why: approve-batch filtered its targets on the raw --org value, so with THREATLOCKER_ORG_ID=A and pending rows in tenants A and B a live run sent an approval under B's header as well. The write now resolves the tenant the way the HTTP client does and fails closed without one. Reads keep the documented rule (tenant_scope.go): THREATLOCKER_ORG_ID scopes live calls but never hides local rows, because an MSP sets it to its parent organization and child-tenant rows carry the child ids. Every member reads the tenant through one of the two helpers, never the raw flag. Every local read declares pp:data-source=local, and TestEveryLocalReadHonoursAnExplicitOrg walks the real command tree so a new local read is checked against --org the day it is added (applications hunt had been missed).

handfixes.summary: approvals approve-batch re-reads each request live (ApprovalRequestGetById, uncached, under its tenant) right before approving it, and approves only requests ThreatLocker still reports pending for that hash
handfixes.why: sync fetches approvals with statusId=1 and prunes only on --full, so a request a technician approved or ignored stays pending in the local store after a plain sync. approve-batch built its plan from those rows and permitted the file in a tenant where the request had been ignored (reproduced: 2 approvals sent under the ignoring tenant). Any ambiguous answer (error, non-object, missing or repeated statusId, hash or tenant mismatch) skips the target.

handfixes.summary: the generated command lists (which.go, root.go, MCP tools.go) describe applications hunt, audit export and audit retention-check by what they read, not as a live file locator or an archiver
handfixes.why: The research descriptions said hunt locates a file 'across every tenant and endpoint' (it reads approval requests and application rules only) and that audit export persists the log locally (audit pull does; export writes out what pull saved). Fix the research manuscript descriptions upstream so a reprint emits these strings.

retired.reason: tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 builds a per-command blocked set (blockedDestinationFlags, blockedInputFlags, root control-plane flags), removes those flags from each tool's schema, refuses any undeclared argument name (so "db=/path" is refused) and skips '=' names in cliArgsFromMCP.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.
tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #5041 (4.33.6): trustees are resolved to SIDs (LA through the OS) and compared by SID; the press generates the alias tests.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #5041 (4.33.6): the DACL section's flags and ACE list are framed (daclFlagsRe, aceListRe), so a NULL DACL behind flags is refused.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
